title: $k$-fold unbiased measurements and maximal incompatibility
abstract: Mutually unbiased bases capture perfect complementarity between two quantum measurements. Extensions beyond pairwise unbiasedness have been proposed, but essentially no non-trivial higher-order constructions are known. We introduce $k$-fold unbiased measurements ($k$-UMs), extending the $k$-fold unbiased bases notion of [arXiv:1706.04446] from rank-one basis measurements to arbitrary-rank projective measurements, and show that this higher-rank setting supports a much richer theory. We develop the notions of algebraic and spectral $k$-UMs and prove that they coincide for rank-one measurements and triples of measurements (3-UMs). We establish strong no-go results for higher-order rank-one constructions and three-outcome 3-UMs, but obtain infinitely many higher-rank triples using Hadamard matrices and Clifford algebras. We then give these structures an exact operational interpretation in terms of measurement incompatibility. For 3-UMs with any number of outcomes, we determine their generalised incompatibility robustness exactly and construct an explicit joint measurement for their noisy versions at the compatibility threshold. Finally, we implement the symmetry reduction of the sum-of-squares hierarchy recently introduced in [New J. Phys. 28, 064509 (2026)] and give numerical evidence that the noise thresholds arising from the $k$-UM analysis may characterise the asymptotic behaviour of this hierarchy. In particular, with very high precision, we numerically show that our constructed four-outcome 3-UMs are among the most incompatible triples of four-outcome measurements.
summary: This paper introduces $k$-fold unbiased measurements ($k$-UMs) to generalize the concept of MUBs to higher-order and higher-rank measurements. The authors develop mathematical tools, including generalized incompatibility robustness, to quantify how incompatible these measurements can be. The work establishes key existence theorems and provides deep structural insights into the limits of quantum measurement theory.
main_problem: The paper extends the concept of mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) to higher-order, higher-rank measurements, studying $k$-fold unbiased measurements ($k$-UMs) and their connection to maximal measurement incompatibility.
main_result: They establish strong no-go results for higher-order rank-one constructions and determine the exact generalized incompatibility robustness for 3-UMs, while also providing explicit constructions using Hadamard matrices.
method: The authors develop algebraic and spectral definitions for $k$-UMs, quantify incompatibility using generalized robustness ($\eta_g(A)$) via SDPs, and employ advanced techniques like sum-of-squares hierarchies and symmetry reduction.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Positive Operator-Valued Measures (POVMs) representing quantum measurements on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, specifically analyzing tuples of measurements (3-UMs).
key_observables: Generalized incompatibility robustness ($\eta_g(A)$), the universal lower bound $\chi_g^k(n)$, and the spectral parameter $\lambda_{k,n}$.
important_parameters: The order of unbiasedness ($k$), the number of outcomes ($n$), and the rank of the measurements.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing structural relations between algebraic and spectral definitions, and uses SDP formulations to derive bounds on incompatibility.
figures_summary: The notes mention Tables II and III, which summarize the sizes of the SDPs after symmetry reduction and compare computed incompatibility bounds ($\chi_g^{k,t}(n)$) against conjectured universal lower bounds ($\lambda_{k,n}/k$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining $k$-UMs, developing algebraic and spectral characterizations, proving structural equivalences and non-existence theorems, and finally applying these concepts to determine exact incompatibility values and analyze the convergence of related mathematical hierarchies.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework developed for characterizing measurement incompatibility provides deep insights into the fundamental limits of quantum measurement theory, which underpins quantum information protocols.
